The reverse ordered edgeParameter is proved equal to the second actual Cramer parameter. The endpoint distance is the parameter from the beginning of g in case A and one minus the parameter on f in case B. Direct determinant algebra gives distance=−det(edge(j−1),edge j)/Delta in both cases. At the centre the endpoint distance is zero and the other parameter is strictly between zero and one, obtained from the actual strict affine betweenness. Nonzero Delta gives continuous actual line-intersection parameters and one neighbourhood with fixed nonzero Delta sign, absolute endpoint distance below one, and the other parameter interior. At nearby G1 tuples the already proved geometric criterion equates raw IsCrossing with both parameters interior. Thus crossing is equivalent to positive endpoint distance and then to turn j=−sign Delta. In case B the bound on one minus the f-parameter supplies its other strict bound; no infinite-line intersection is silently treated as a segment crossing.

The other needle-corner determinant is an actual negative multiple of Delta: in A the multiplier is t−1 for the strict central betweenness parameter t, and in B it is −t. Its nonzero central sign therefore persists as −sign Delta. The crossing criterion gives both needle turns equal to turn j in the crossing case. In the noncrossing case, G1 makes turn j nonzero; its only remaining sign is +sign Delta, yielding opposite needle turns. The order of the two named corners is handled separately in A and B. No assertion assumes that the two signs might be zero or that the central tuple is generic.
